evidence_boundaries: Sonnet, Opus, and GPT-5.5 rows use post-hoc best-of-six HLS-synthesis selection and stored HLSFactory baseline cycles.
Sonnet aggregates use the 25-kernel all-arm common set; the displayed Doitgen row has only four of six agentic setups.
The teacher-model candidates lack independent output comparison and generated-design RTL simulation.
The GPT-5.5 source records use only the model key gpt55 and do not record an exact checkpoint revision.
GPT-5.5 aggregates use 23 kernels with all six agentic setups attempted; three displayed kernels have one unexecuted setup.
DeepSeek and Grok bars divide executed benchmark-baseline RTL cycles by fixed-flash reported RTL cycles; executed baselines cover 26 kernels and are unavailable for Heat-3D and Seidel-2D.
The common-cohort table intersects the executed baseline, passing expertise-on/off arms, and the primary-selection cohort.
Experiment metadata identifies both enabled RTL arms as the all-skills policy. The compact DeepSeek campaign key is aav_n (all positive plus avoid rules), while the Grok input labels the arm skills.
Five Grok rows with asymmetric enabled-arm repeat selection are shown but excluded from the strict aggregate.
The five rows share kernel positions and improvement direction, not a common evidence level, search budget, or expertise snapshot.
